container: Climate change is reshaping the planet through rising temperatures and shifting weather patterns. Burning coal, oil, and gas releases greenhouse gases that trap heat in the atmosphere. As average temperatures climb, glaciers shrink, sea levels rise, and heat waves become more frequent and severe. Many regions face longer droughts, while others experience heavier rainfall and destructive floods. These changes threaten crops, freshwater supplies, homes, and public health. Warmer oceans can damage coral reefs and strengthen some storms. Wildlife must adapt, migrate, or risk extinction as habitats change faster than many species can manage. Climate impacts are not shared equally. Poor communities often have fewer resources to prepare for disasters or rebuild afterward. Children, older adults, and people with existing health conditions are especially vulnerable to heat and disease. Reducing emissions is essential. Governments can expand clean energy, improve public transportation, protect forests, and make buildings more efficient. Individuals can conserve energy, waste less food, and support climate friendly policies. Adaptation also matters. Cities need shade trees, reliable emergency plans, and resilient infrastructure. Cooperation across nations can accelerate innovation and provide funding for vulnerable regions. Choices made today will shape future generations.
